notes: Hand-vetted Truth or Dare challenges. Every entry has been manually reviewed against the safety rules in TRUTH_OR_DARE_PLAN.md §4. Each entry is keyed by (subject, gradeBand, tier, category) for lookup. Used as the always-on fallback when AI generation fails moderation or times out.

entries.prompt: Name the three main stages of the water cycle in any order.
entries.teacherHint: Accept evaporation, condensation, and precipitation in any order.

entries.prompt: Mime the water cycle in 30 seconds — include evaporation, condensation, and precipitation. Your team will narrate what you're doing.
entries.teacherHint: Look for: rising-arms gesture (evaporation), gathering gesture (condensation), falling fingers (precipitation).

entries.prompt: You are a single water droplet. In 30 seconds, narrate your trip from the ocean to a raincloud — out loud, including at least 3 stages.
entries.teacherHint: Listen for: evaporation, rising air, cooling, condensation.

entries.prompt: If you cut a pizza into 8 equal slices and eat 3, what fraction did you eat?
entries.teacherHint: 3/8 (also accept 'three eighths').

entries.prompt: Explain in one sentence why dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal.
entries.teacherHint: Look for: 'because we're undoing the division' or 'because fractions less than 1 make things bigger when you divide'.

entries.prompt: Convince us in 30 seconds that a triangle is the strongest shape — for engineers. Use at least one real example.
entries.teacherHint: Bridges, roof trusses, geodesic domes — any one works.

entries.prompt: Without looking at notes, name two causes of the French Revolution.
entries.teacherHint: Fiscal crisis, food prices, loss of legitimacy, Enlightenment ideas — any two.

entries.prompt: Defend the storming of the Bastille from Louis XVI's perspective. 60 seconds — stay in character, concede ONE point your peasants got right.
entries.teacherHint: Listen for: fiscal crisis, food prices, OR loss of legitimacy — any one earns full credit.

entries.prompt: Defend the position that the printing press was the most important invention of the past 1000 years — in 30 seconds.
entries.teacherHint: Listen for: spread of literacy, Reformation, Scientific Revolution, mass communication.

entries.prompt: Be a defense lawyer for one character in a book you've read this year. 45 seconds. Argue mitigating circumstances.
entries.teacherHint: Any book they've read; coherence and character knowledge are the bar.

entries.prompt: Make up a one-sentence summary of any fairy tale — but in the style of a sports announcer.
entries.teacherHint: Recognizable tale + recognizable sportscaster voice.

entries.prompt: In 30 seconds, draw a circuit on the board WITH YOUR EYES CLOSED. The class will judge.
entries.teacherHint: Battery + wire + bulb in some kind of loop is the bar.

entries.prompt: What's one thing you understand best from this unit, and one thing you still wish was clearer?
entries.teacherHint: Genuine reflection — no wrong answer.

entries.prompt: If we picked up where this lesson left off in 10 years, what's one thing about it that will probably have changed?
entries.teacherHint: Coherent prediction grounded in the content; not 'I don't know'.

entries.prompt: Pitch the topic we just learned to a 5-year-old. 30 seconds. Use one toy or food as a metaphor.
entries.teacherHint: Accuracy + clarity for the target age, not perfect simplicity.

entries.prompt: You are a single muscle fiber contracting. In 25 seconds, become it — physically and verbally. We'll guess which type (skeletal / smooth / cardiac).
entries.teacherHint: Recognizable contraction motion + correct guess from class.

entries.prompt: You're a sailor on Columbus's ship in 1492. In 45 seconds, complain about ONE specific thing without naming the year, the captain, or the destination.
entries.teacherHint: Historically plausible complaint (food, length of voyage, mutiny tension, scurvy).

entries.prompt: Mime a number from 0 to 20 using ONLY one hand. Class guesses.
entries.teacherHint: Counting with fingers + clear indication. No speaking.

entries.prompt: Tell us about a time something we covered in this unit reminded you of real life.
entries.teacherHint: Coherence + a specific moment — no wrong answer.

entries.prompt: Name the four chambers of the heart.
entries.teacherHint: Left atrium, right atrium, left ventricle, right ventricle.
acceptableAnswers: left atrium right atrium left ventricle right ventricle
atria and ventricles, left and right of each

entries.prompt: In one sentence, explain why the American colonies wanted to break from Britain.
entries.teacherHint: Taxation without representation, distance / autonomy, Enlightenment ideas — any solid one works.

entries.prompt: Make up a 4-line rap about the topic we just covered. 30 seconds — rhymes optional, energy not.
entries.teacherHint: Recognizable topic + clear rhythm; bonus laughs for confidence.

entries.prompt: Tell us the plot of your favourite book — but in 20 seconds. Go.
entries.teacherHint: Beginning, middle, end — clear arc beats accuracy.

entries.prompt: Predict ONE specific way human biology might change in the next 200 years if global temperatures rise 4°C. 40 seconds, evidence-based.
entries.teacherHint: Solid prediction with biological reasoning — heat tolerance, skin pigmentation, body size, etc.
